# usbless-dualboot

> Install Windows alongside Linux without a USB stick, by using the internal SSD as the installer and restoring a clean dual-boot menu.

Project type: system administration CLI (bash).
License: MIT.
Status: 0.2.0, guarded storage phases with isolated regression tests; generalized installer phases still need VM/hardware validation.

## What it does
- Probes disks, partitions, filesystems, encryption (LUKS), bootloader (Limine/GRUB/systemd-boot), firmware (UEFI/TPM/Secure Boot).
- Plans a safe shrink of the Linux storage (filesystem -> LUKS -> partition).
- Creates a temporary FAT32 installer partition, copies a Windows ISO, and splits sources/install.wim with wimlib so it fits FAT32.
- Registers a one-time UEFI boot entry for the internal installer.
- After Windows installs: restores the default boot order, adds a Windows entry to the boot menu, and can set up Secure Boot with sbctl.

## Entry points
- README.md - overview, quickstart, supported matrix, safety.
- SKILL.md - agent skill: when to use, guardrails, exact workflow.
- docs/SAFETY.md - destructive-operation policy and recovery.
- docs/DESIGN.md - architecture, phase model, portability.
- docs/SECUREBOOT.md - signing the Linux boot chain and enrolling keys.
- bin/usbless-dualboot - CLI dispatcher (help, version, subcommands).
- lib/probe.sh - read-only detection with --json.
- lib/plan.sh - plan generation.
- src/Main.qml, src/backend.cpp - optional native Qt Quick app using the same engine.
- bin/build-ui / bin/test-ui / bin/install-ui - build, offscreen GUI tests and Arch package installation.
- docs/GUI.md - graphical workflow, state/privilege model, keyboard shortcuts and validation limits.
- platforms/windows/Usbless.Windows.csproj - Windows-native .NET Framework application and embedded PowerShell engine.
- data/catalog.json, docs/COVERAGE.md - implemented recipes, planned entries and version-specific evidence.
- docs/VM-LAB.md - disposable VM setup, cached media, diagnostics and test-payload refresh.

## Directions
- add-windows (implemented): Linux machine gains Windows.
- add-linux (beta): Linux-hosted GRUB loopback carrier; see docs/DIRECTIONS.md. Not a Windows-native app.

## Commands
  usbless-dualboot probe [--json]
  usbless-dualboot doctor [--json]
  usbless-dualboot verify --iso PATH [--sha256 HASH] [--json]
  usbless-dualboot status [--json]
  usbless-dualboot guide
  usbless-dualboot plan --add windows|linux --iso PATH --linux-new-size SIZE [--write]
  usbless-dualboot shrink [--dry-run]
  usbless-dualboot stage [--dry-run]
  usbless-dualboot boot (--installer | --restore | --cancel) [--dry-run]
  usbless-dualboot windows (--add | --remove)
  usbless-dualboot secureboot (--prep | --enroll | --verify)

## Hard rules for agents
1. Never run shrink/stage/boot/secureboot without first showing the user `probe` and `plan` output.
2. Never hardcode device names; resolve them from `probe --json`.
3. Mutating commands must be run with sudo in a visible terminal (the user enters the password).
4. Take backups (GPT, LUKS header) before any partition or encryption change.
5. If the user is dual-booting Windows, warn about BitLocker/Device Encryption recovery keys before changing Secure Boot keys or state.
6. Disabling Secure Boot may recover unsigned-loader failures; it does not repair storage damage.
7. Use one config across runs. Inspect interrupted phases and backups; do not blindly retry.
8. Linux has guarded offline ext4 shrink and ownership-based installer cleanup, with VM storage-fixture evidence. Automatic undo, filesystem growth and second-disk planning remain unavailable. See docs/OFFLINE-EXT4.md and docs/COVERAGE.md for the exact validation boundary. Windows-native implementation is under platforms/windows.

Large Casper ISOs require an NTFS carrier: Kubuntu 26.10's actual initramfs scanner
does not accept exFAT. `repair-carrier --dry-run [--iso VERIFIED-RELOCATED-SOURCE]`
reviews migration of a completed owned exFAT Linux carrier. Actual migration needs
`--confirm-rebuild-installer`, preserves GPT/OS/EFI and completion markers, and
retains an interruption marker on failure. Do not rerun stage or clear markers.
See docs/RECOVERY.md and docs/validation/kubuntu-26.10-casper-root-cause.json.

## Environment assumptions
- Linux in UEFI mode, GPT disk.
- Btrfs (online shrink) or ext4 (offline shrink); optionally LUKS2.
- A Windows 11 ISO supplied by the user.
